title: FlatRestrictionOrdinaryComparisons
statement: For a flat ringed diagram input x [def-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-input] and a small category J, there exist ordinary natural isomorphisms b0:inverseS⋙restrictU ≅ restrictV⋙inverseR and d0:directS⋙restrictV ≅ restrictU⋙directR. On each diagram component their underlying maps obey exactly OrdinaryComparisonsNormalized: b0 is the composite of the S inverse-image comparison, sameInverse, and the inverse R comparison; d0 is the analogous direct-image comparison through sameDirect. No derived-category assertion is included.

source.place: Tag 03D3, naturality of the geometric adjunction

proof.text: Compose the underlying inverse-image module isomorphisms through sameInverse. The operation comparison equations give additivity; the coefficient square gives R-linearity. The inverse is linear by the inverse identities. Naturality of those comparisons gives an isomorphism b0 on diagrams, retaining every J arrow.

source.place: Tag 03D3, naturality of the geometric adjunction

proof.text: Form the direct comparison as the mate of b0 inverse under the termwise module adjunctions. Apply the general adjunct-mate identity to the S counit; its transpose is the identity. The inverse normalization of b0, the two input transpose equations, and sameAdjunction give the direct underlying-sheaf normalization. Its underlying map is an isomorphism by that equation. The underlying-set functor reflects isomorphisms, hence the mate is an isomorphism on every diagram component, every diagram and therefore as a natural transformation. This constructs d0 with the required normalization.

theorem flatRestriction_ordinary_comparisons :
    ∃ (b0 : x.inverseS J ⋙ x.restrictU J ≅ x.restrictV J ⋙ x.inverseR J)
      (d0 : x.directS J ⋙ x.restrictV J ≅ x.restrictU J ⋙ x.directR J),
      x.OrdinaryComparisonsNormalized J b0 d0
